name: InfluxData, Inc. (formerly Errplane)
origin_detail: Founded in 2012 as Errplane, a Y Combinator-backed company; founder and CTO Paul Dix created InfluxDB, which Errplane began developing as open source in late 2013 (first release 2013-09-24). Renamed InfluxData in late 2015. HQ San Francisco; remote-first.
openness_notes: InfluxDB was MIT-licensed. In 2016 InfluxData announced clustering would be sold only as closed-source software (InfluxDB Enterprise): open core (2). InfluxDB 3 Open Source (Core) entered public alpha on 2025-01-13 under MIT/Apache-2.0, with limits (five databases, no compactor) and a proprietary InfluxDB 3 Enterprise. Its CLA lets InfluxData relicense contributions, including closed-source.

license_history.license: MIT core; clustering only in closed-source InfluxDB Enterprise
license_history.note: InfluxData blog dated 2016-03-10 (Wikipedia text says May 2016).

license_history.license: InfluxDB 3 Core under MIT/Apache-2.0; InfluxDB 3 Enterprise proprietary

relicensing_events.outcome_note: A feature moved out of the open edition, not a licence change; community reaction was mixed (Wikipedia). No major fork found.

risk_events: 2016: Clustering removed from open-source InfluxDB, mixed community reaction
2025: InfluxDB 3 Core shipped with limits that steer larger users to Enterprise
robustness: Single vendor, with a CLA that permits closed-source relicensing of contributions; the core (InfluxDB 3 Core, Telegraf) remains MIT/Apache and forkable. The company cites 2,600+ enterprise customers and 1.3M+ active InfluxDB instances.
openness_effect_assessment: InfluxData never moved its core off OSI licences; it monetized by withholding features (clustering in 2016, scale limits in InfluxDB 3 Core). That avoided a licence fight but drew complaints, and its funding grew modestly, from an $8.1M Series A (2014) to a $51M equity Series E (2023), with no disclosed valuation.
key_takeaway: InfluxData is 'closing by feature' rather than by licence: the code stays MIT/Apache, but the features enterprises need are paid. It avoided forks, but its modest funding and undisclosed valuation point to a smaller outcome than peers that relicensed or went public.

sources.title: InfluxData closes Series E round
sources.supports: funding (Series E $51M equity + $30M debt, led by Princeville Capital and Citi Ventures; 1,900+ commercial customers)
